realm.name: ADMIN
realm.description: May approve and reject orders. Maps to ROLE_ADMIN via the realm_access.roles claim.

realm.name: CUSTOMER
realm.description: May place, read and cancel their own orders.

realm.name: SERVICE
realm.description: A service acting on its own behalf rather than a user's. Held by service accounts only, and what inventory's reservation and stock-reserve endpoints accept from a caller with no customer behind it - an order released because a Kafka event withdrew the product.

clients.name: MCP server (service account)
clients.description: Confidential client for the MCP server. Service accounts only: it has no user behind it, so it takes a token with the client-credentials grant and never a login. Its own account holds ADMIN and CUSTOMER, which is what lets the write tools approve an order and place one.

clients.name: Orders service (service account)
clients.description: Confidential client for the orders service, used only when it calls inventory with no user behind the call - a Kafka event withdrawing a product makes it release the holds on the orders that wanted it, and there is no request to relay a token from. Its account holds SERVICE and nothing else: it can take and give back stock, and cannot touch the catalogue. A call that *does* have a user behind it relays that user's own token instead, so this identity never stands in for a customer.
